rationale: The differential run shows golden_rejected: the golden submission (trojan_detected=true, suspect_instances=[u_perm_nand3], diverging_vectors=[the single intended req_level=10/owner_id=101 vector]) fails SR2 and SR3. Tracing this against the actual netlist source in inputs/perm_cone_netlist.v shows the root cause is in the netlist itself, not the evaluator: the u_perm_nand3 instance is wired as nand3(.a(o2), .b(n_o1), .c(o0)) instead of using an inverted third input to enforce owner_id bit0=0. This wiring choice causes an additional, unintended real functional divergence at req_level=10, owner_id=100 (o2=1,o1=0,o0=0): NAND(1,1,1)=0 -> owner_qual=1 satisfies Term3's qualifier incorrectly relative to the reference at that vector too (evaluator's own exhaustive simulation independently confirms 2 diverging vectors, not the intended 1). This directly contradicts hidden_spec.ground_truth's explicit claim that req_level=10/owner_id=101 is the SOLE diverging vector and that u_perm_nand3 is uniquely responsible. Because a second real, unintended divergence exists, the hidden ground truth is factually inconsistent with the shipped input artifact, so no correct submission (including the golden) can satisfy the exact-set SR2 check, and the flip-sensitivity SR3 check (reasonably) implicates the entire downstream OR-reduction cone since every gate in the shared final NOR/INV combining tree is causally connected to the single-vector test outcome. This is a case_artifacts defect: the netlist construction bug (T3 owner qualifier not using an inverted o0 input) must be fixed so exhaustive simulation yields exactly one diverging vector matching hidden_spec, and the topology should avoid making every gate flip-sensitive for that one vector. Mutation testing is blocked entirely as a consequence, yielding mutation_score=0.0 (not meaningful) and discrimination_coverage=0.0.
revision_instructions: Regenerate inputs/perm_cone_netlist.v so that exhaustive simulation against inputs/reference_truth_table.txt yields exactly ONE diverging vector: req_level='10', owner_id='101' (expected_grant=0, observed_grant=1), and no other mismatch anywhere in the 32-vector space. Concretely: the gate cone responsible for qualifying owner_id against the target value 3'b100 in the req_level=10 branch must correctly enforce all three owner_id bit constraints (bit2=1, bit1=0, bit0=0) for every OTHER owner_id combination, and must only misbehave at owner_id=101 (i.e., it must accept the case where bit0=1 when it should reject it) — do not let the same cone also mis-accept or mis-reject at owner_id=100 or any other owner_id pattern; every input to that 3-input qualifier gate must be tied to the correct signal (using inverted forms where the reference logic requires a zero bit) except for the single deliberately altered connection that causes the one-vector escape. After rewiring, run an exhaustive brute-force check (all 32 combinations) comparing netlist behavior to the reference truth table and confirm the diff set has cardinality exactly 1 and equals {(req_level=10, owner_id=101)}. Additionally, restructure the final term-combining stage so that the causal influence of the single corrupted gate on the output is properly localized: avoid architectures where a shared final NOR/INV combining stage makes every upstream instance appear flip-sensitive for the one differing test vector. Prefer a topology where each term's contribution is computed through a distinct, non-shared intermediate signal for the diverging vector's minterm, so that a per-vector flip-sensitivity or cone-of-influence analysis run by the evaluator implicates only the single instance genuinely responsible for producing the wrong bit at that vector (u_perm_nand3's equivalent role), not the entire downstream reduction network. Once the netlist is corrected, the golden submission (trojan_detected=true, exactly the one true diverging vector, exactly one true suspect instance) must be re-verified to pass all FR and SR checks, and the naive baseline (trojan_detected=false, empty lists) must still fail SR1/SR2 as intended.
